text:
maya: Quick follow-up from the congestion + fairness sync — we still need a concrete handoff API between ingress (frontdoor) and admission-service. question: do we push tight telemetry + intents to admission, or keep a pull/publish model?

sam: leaning push for low-latency decisions. ingress already has hot view of queue lengths and p95. if admission can act on a compact signal we can avoid extra rpc on every request. :thinking:

jordan: push is fine but we need to throttle signals. signal storms (every worker spamming p95) will cause thrash. propose a 1s aggregated envelope per tenant and a jittered publish window.

li: coupling concern — ingress shouldn't be allowed to mutate tenant quotas directly. abuse detector may want to suggest "abuse_score" and admission should be sole authority to change quotas/penalties. 

sam: agreed. design idea: a small proto where ingress offers an aggregated "congestion envelope" and admission responds with a lightweight decision(token_limit, shed_mode, weight_mod). sketch: 

```proto
service AdmissionHandoff {
  rpc OfferEnvelope(Envelope) returns (Decision) {}
}
message Envelope {
  string tenant = 1;
  int64 tokens_in_flight = 2;
  float p95_latency_ms = 3;
  int32 pending_requests = 4;
  float abuse_score = 5; // optional, 0..1
}
message Decision {
  int32 allowed_tokens = 1;
  string mode = 2; // "normal" | "soft-shed" | "evict"
  float fairness_weight = 3;
}
```

jordan: +1 to that proto but add a checksum/version field so we can roll upgrade policies without breaking old ingresses.

li: important: admission should mediate any penalty. instead of raw booleans, ingress should only send signals and optionally a trusted "anomaly_flag" from our abuse-detector service. admission runs the policy.

maya: ok so pattern: ingress -> OfferEnvelope (aggregated per-second), admission -> Decision. admission can call back to a central ledger for leases if it needs to enforce longer-lived capacity windows.

sam: what about backpressure signals to clients? semantic: 429 for client-rate exceed, 503 for short-term capacity (we're overloaded). we should standardize headers: X-Redwood-Decision: soft-shed or evict + X-Redwood-Estimate-ms.

jordan: also need to decide whether admission returns immediate token_delta (credit model) vs allowed_tokens (absolute cap). credit model helps bursty workloads.

li: abuse path: if abuse_score > 0.9 admission should map to probation with probation_ttl and reduced fairness_weight. do not allow ingress to bypass that.

sam: sample config snippet for runtime policy (for ops/console):

```yaml
admission_policy: congestion-shepherd-v1
signals: [p95_ms, tokens_in_flight, pending_requests, abuse_score]
aggregation_window_ms: 1000
jitter_pct: 10
fallback: soft-shed
response_mode: allowed_tokens # or credit_delta
```

mike: (ops-bot) deploy-bot: rolling canary of admission v2 will start tomorrow at 08:00 UTC, watch slo-alerts. :eyes:

jordan: curious about observability — we need token-level tracing so we can replay and debug weird throttle events. add a trace_id in Envelope/Decision payloads.

maya: noted. also need a circuit for stale admission decisions: ingress should accept a TTL on Decision and fall back to local conservative limits if stale.

li: TL;DR risks: coupling, signal storms, and inadvertent trust. mitigations: 1) aggregated envelopes only, 2) admission is authoritative for penalties, 3) versioned proto + ttl on decisions, 4) audit logs for every eviction/penalty.

sam: implementation plan proposal: phase 1: proto + ingress aggregator + admission read-only decisions (no long-lived leases). phase 2: add lease API and probation path + audits. phase 3: abuse-detector tight integration and console controls.

maya: action items:
- @sam: write draft proto + small server stub for handoff (owner) — due Wed EOD
- @jordan: design aggregation/jitter helpers and perf budget (owner) — due Thu
- @li: abuse integration contract + signal schema (owner) — due Thu
- @maya: produce rollout playbook (canary + rollback) and observability checklist — due Fri

mike: acked, will wire alerting channels and bring the canary config.

maya: thanks all. adding this thread to the follow-up RFC doc. :thumbsup:
